newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Security tight ahead of Manley funeral in Jamaica.
newsitem.headline: Security tight ahead of Manley funeral in Jamaica.

text.p: Jamaica stepped up security on Saturday ahead of a state funeral for former Prime Minister Michael Manley that is expected to be attended by a throng of dignitaries, including Cuban President Fidel Castro.
Sunday's funeral follows two days of mourning in which tens of thousands of people crowded Kingston's national arena where Manley's body lay in state.

The official news agency Jampress said Castro was due to arrive at Kingston's airport at 11 a.m. on Sunday. Other dignitaries expected at the funeral are, among others, former U.S. President Jimmy Carter, former Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere and former Venezuelan president Carlos Andres Perez.

Perez and Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan were among those who filed past Manley's body on Saturday during extended viewing hours to accommodate the huge numbers of people who lined up to pay their respects.
Manley's burial will be the first state funeral in 20 years in Jamaica -- the last one was in 1977 for former prime minister, and Manley's cousin, Sir Alexander Bustamante.
Jamaica's defence and police forces have called out all reservists, along with veterans, officer cadets, the Boy Scouts and Girl Guides and even nurses to maintain order along the funeral route.
The funeral is due to be held at the Catholic cathedral a short distance from National Heroes Park, where Manley's body will be interred.
Manley died on March 6 at home, aged 72, after a long struggle with cancer.
